title: FMGE PSM Mock 1 - Section 1
subject: Community Medicine
description: FMGE-style 50-question PSM section generated from the reviewed Day 2 PSM source.

questions.stem: The routine cold-chain temperature range shown for maintenance of vaccines from manufacture until administration is:
questions.explanation: The cold-chain page explicitly shows vaccine temperature maintenance from manufacture until administration at +2°C to +8°C.

questions.stem: Which chemical is associated with the Vizag industrial gas tragedy in the notes?
questions.explanation: The Vizag tragedy is annotated as styrene gas. Methyl isocyanate is associated on the same page with Bhopal, making it the closest distractor.

questions.stem: According to the Rangarajan Committee figure shown in the notes, the urban per-capita poverty-line expenditure threshold is:
questions.explanation: The Rangarajan Committee annotation gives rural <₹32 and urban <₹47/person/day. The rural ₹32 figure is the main competing option.

questions.stem: In ICD-11, “Mental, Behavioral, or Neurodevelopmental Disorders” are shown under:
questions.explanation: The source places mental, behavioral and neurodevelopmental disorders in Chapter 06. Chapter 21 is separately annotated for disorders of unknown etiology.

questions.stem: Which diluent is shown for reconstitution of BCG vaccine?
questions.explanation: The source table pairs BCG with normal saline (NaCl). Distilled water is shown for measles/MR/MMR, while PBS is shown for JE. Always reconstitute a vaccine with the diluent supplied for it.

questions.stem: Which strain is shown for the live Japanese encephalitis vaccine?
questions.explanation: The live JE strain is SA-14-14-2; Nakayama is shown for killed JE.

questions.stem: The date shown for global eradication of smallpox is:
questions.explanation: The source explicitly gives 08 May 1980 for smallpox eradication.

questions.stem: Which tablet-based application is shown as being used by ANMs for RCH data entry?
questions.explanation: ANMOL is described as ANM On Line, a tablet-based software system used for RCH data entry.

questions.stem: Which indigenous COVID-19 vaccine in the notes is administered by the intranasal route?
questions.explanation: iNCOVACC is shown as an intranasal vaccine, administered as drops into the nostrils.

questions.stem: The dose of Human Rabies Immunoglobulin shown in the notes is:
questions.explanation: HRIG is shown at 20 IU/kg; ERIG is shown at 40 IU/kg, which is the key discriminator.

questions.stem: The interval between symptom onset in a primary case and symptom onset in the linked secondary case is termed:
questions.explanation: Serial interval is the gap between the onset of the primary case and the onset of the secondary case. Generation time is separately defined on the page as extending from organism entry to maximum infectivity.

questions.stem: Approximately how many vaccine vials can the vaccine carrier shown in the notes hold?
questions.explanation: The vaccine carrier is annotated as holding approximately 16–20 vaccine vials.

questions.stem: The RCH programme is shown as beginning in:
questions.explanation: The sequence shown is NFPP 1951 → CSSM 1992 → RCH 1997.

questions.stem: The Anemia Mukt Bharat tablet shown contains:
questions.explanation: The displayed tablet composition is 60 mg iron + 500 µg folic acid.

questions.stem: The vitamin A solution shown has a strength of:
questions.explanation: The solution strength is explicitly shown as 1 lakh IU/mL.

questions.stem: After a single banquet meal, cases of acute gastroenteritis rise sharply and then fall sharply, with the cluster confined to one incubation period. Which epidemic pattern best fits?
questions.explanation: A sudden rise and fall with cases clustered within one incubation period is the pattern shown for a single-exposure point source.

questions.stem: Residents repeatedly draw water from the same contaminated well over several days. The epidemic curve develops successive waves corresponding to repeated exposure. This is:
questions.explanation: Repeated exposure to the same contaminated source produces repeated waves.

questions.stem: A multipurpose worker visits households once every fortnight to actively search for malaria cases. This is:
questions.explanation: The slide specifically places malaria MPW-M household activity once per fortnight under active surveillance. Passive surveillance waits for spontaneous reporting.

questions.stem: A healthy motorcyclist routinely wears a helmet to reduce injury risk. According to the prevention examples in the notes, this is:
questions.explanation: Seat belt/helmet use is located under primary specific protection. The person is healthy and protection is being applied before disease/injury occurs.

questions.stem: An 18-month-old child presents for routine immunization. According to the 16-24 month row of the national schedule shown in the notes, which vaccine set is due?
options: MR2 + DPT booster + OPV booster + JE2
BCG + OPV0 + Hepatitis B birth dose
DPT2 + OPV2 + Hepatitis B2 + Hib2 + RVV2
questions.explanation: The 16-24 month row of the immunization schedule shows MR2, DPT booster, OPV booster, and JE2. The birth-dose set belongs to the at-birth row, while the DPT2/OPV2/HepB2/Hib2/RVV2 set belongs to 10 weeks.
questions.answer_label: MR2 + DPT booster + OPV booster + JE2
questions.answer: MR2 + DPT booster + OPV booster + JE2

questions.stem: After a road-traffic accident, a man loses his right hand and can no longer drive or write. His inability to perform those activities represents:
questions.explanation: Loss of the hand is the impairment; inability to write or drive is the disability. Handicap appears when the person cannot fulfil the expected social role.

questions.stem: During an outbreak investigation, the patient who first brings the disease to the investigator's attention is the:
questions.explanation: The index case is the first case coming to the investigator's notice. It does not necessarily have to be the primary case.

questions.stem: A public-health strategy explicitly integrates reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health. Which framework shown in the notes matches this description?
questions.explanation: The strategy diagram expands RMNCH+A into reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health. The decisive clue is the explicit addition of adolescent health.

questions.stem: Healthy contacts of a case are detained until the maximum incubation period has elapsed. This is:
questions.explanation: Quarantine applies to healthy contacts and extends to the maximum incubation period. Isolation applies to cases and continues until recovery.

questions.stem: Among 250 cases of a disease, 10 patients die. Using the formula shown in the notes, the case-fatality rate is:
questions.explanation: Formula: deaths among cases / total cases ×100. 10/250 × 100 = 4%.

questions.stem: A vaccine vial monitor has an inner square clearly lighter than the surrounding outer circle, and the expiry date has not passed. What should be done?
questions.explanation: The VVM diagram marks the lighter-inner-square stages as usable. The later darkened stages are marked unusable.

questions.stem: A previously unvaccinated person presents immediately after a bleeding dog bite. What is the first local wound-care step shown in the notes?
options: Wash vigorously with soap and water for 15–20 minutes
questions.explanation: The rabies wound-management diagram gives soap + water for 15–20 min and marks suturing as contraindicated.
questions.answer_label: Wash with soap and water for 15–20 minutes
questions.answer: Wash vigorously with soap and water for 15–20 minutes

questions.stem: A 24×7 PHC provides all Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care functions. Which requirement would move the patient beyond BEmONC to comprehensive emergency care?
questions.explanation: BEmONC contains the first seven emergency obstetric/newborn functions. Blood transfusion and surgery are additional comprehensive functions.

questions.stem: For a home delivery, the ASHA postnatal schedule shown is:
questions.explanation: For home delivery, the ASHA schedule includes seven visits, beginning on day 1. Institutional delivery begins on day 3 and has six.

questions.stem: Which cold-chain equipment pair is shown at the district/CHC level?
questions.explanation: The district/CHC level is shown with a large ILR and large deep freezer, with approximately one month of storage.

questions.stem: Which vaccine is linked with brachial neuritis on the AEFI chart?
questions.explanation: The AEFI chart associates brachial neuritis with TT/Td. Intussusception is linked with rotavirus vaccine and thrombocytopenia with MMR.

questions.stem: Two districts have the same number of maternal deaths and the same number of live births. District Y, however, has twice as many women aged 15–49 years as District X. Which statement follows from the formulas in the notes?
options: Maternal mortality ratio is lower in District Y
Maternal mortality rate is lower in District Y, while the ratio is unchanged
Both maternal mortality rate and ratio are unchanged
Maternal mortality rate is unchanged, while the ratio is lower
questions.explanation: MMRate uses women aged 15–49 as its denominator, whereas MMRatio uses live births. Doubling only the reproductive-age female denominator lowers the rate while leaving the ratio unchanged.
questions.answer_label: Maternal mortality rate falls; ratio unchanged
questions.answer: Maternal mortality rate is lower in District Y, while the ratio is unchanged

questions.stem: When preparing the ice pack shown in the notes, the correct method is to:
options: Fill to the horizontal water-level line without additives
Fill with warm water immediately before use
questions.explanation: The ice pack shows a horizontal water-level line and explicitly states that nothing should be added to the water.
questions.answer_label: Fill to the line with no additive
questions.answer: Fill to the horizontal water-level line without additives

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl is receiving Cervavac according to the schedule displayed in the source. Which regimen is shown?
questions.explanation: The Cervavac annotation shows 9–14 years: two doses at 0 and 6 months.

questions.stem: Which vaccine matches the following description from the source: killed vaccine, two doses, 4–6 weeks apart, 0.5 mL IM?
questions.explanation: Covaxin is shown as killed, two doses, 4–6 weeks apart, 0.5 mL IM. Covishield is labelled viral-vector based with a longer interval.

questions.stem: An unvaccinated 14-month-old child has household exposure to measles. The child is brought 48 hours after exposure. The notes state that the measles vaccine should be administered within 3 days of exposure to be effective. What is the best action?
questions.explanation: The source states that measles vaccine should be given within 3 days of exposure and separately illustrates the post-exposure timing relationship. At 48 hours, the child remains within that window.

questions.stem: A vial of reconstituted measles vaccine was prepared at 9 AM and the final dose was administered from the same vial at 4 PM. Which vaccine-associated event is the source particularly warning against in this situation?
questions.explanation: The lyophilized-vaccine page says reconstituted vaccine should be used within 4 hours and links failure to this handling rule with TSS; the AEFI chart also associates TSS with measles vaccine.

questions.stem: A region that has been polio-free for years detects one new laboratory-confirmed wild poliovirus case. Given the source definition of an epidemic as occurrence above normal expectation, how should this event be classified?
questions.explanation: The epidemic definition is occurrence clearly above normal expectation. The source also records India as polio-free; therefore a new wild-virus case when the expected background is zero represents epidemic occurrence.

questions.stem: A veterinarian previously completed rabies vaccination and now sustains another rabies-risk bite. After appropriate wound washing, which vaccine regimen is shown for a previously vaccinated person?
options: Two IM doses on days 0 and 3
Five IM doses on days 0, 3, 7, 14 and 28
questions.explanation: The rabies schedule explicitly gives post-exposure in vaccinated: IM day 0 and day 3. The wound-care page supplies the initial washing step already completed in the stem.
questions.answer_label: Two IM doses on days 0 and 3
questions.answer: Two IM doses on days 0 and 3

questions.stem: The notes show that wild poliovirus type 2 had been eradicated before the 2016 switch from trivalent OPV to bivalent OPV, and also annotate circulating VDPV as most commonly type 2. Which explanation best fits the switch?
options: Type 1 was removed because it caused most VAPP
Type 2 antigen could not tolerate routine cold-chain temperature
Wild type 2 had been eradicated while vaccine-derived type 2 remained a concern
OPV was replaced because IPV had become unavailable
questions.explanation: The switch page states that P2 had been eradicated before tOPV was changed to bOPV, while the AEFI/OPV notes identify circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus most commonly with type 2.
questions.answer_label: Wild P2 eradicated while vaccine-derived type 2 remained a concern
questions.answer: Wild type 2 had been eradicated while vaccine-derived type 2 remained a concern

questions.stem: A district records 12 maternal deaths and 30,000 live births in one year. Which pair correctly gives the maternal mortality ratio and the healthcare domain the source associates most directly with that indicator?
questions.explanation: Formula: 12/30,000 × 100,000 = 40. The indicator map associates MMR with maternal care.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman completes only the minimum RCH antenatal schedule and later has an institutional delivery. Which combination correctly matches the minimum antenatal visits and the ASHA postnatal visits shown in the source?
questions.explanation: The ANC page explicitly labels 4 visits as the RCH minimum and separately shows 8 visits for WHO, so the four-visit figure is not being treated as a universal minimum. For institutional delivery, the ASHA schedule shows 6 postnatal visits on days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42.

questions.stem: A subcentre has no fixed cold-chain equipment and needs to take approximately 16–20 vaccine vials for an outreach session lasting less than a day. Which device best fits both facts shown in the source?
questions.explanation: The subcentre has no fixed storage equipment in the hierarchy, while the vaccine carrier is shown as holding 16–20 vials for approximately 12–24 hours.

questions.stem: Which indicator–value pair shown in the notes corresponds to the best indicator of combined maternal and newborn care?
questions.explanation: The indicator table gives PNMR = 18, and the following diagram labels PNMR as the best indicator of combined maternal and newborn care.

questions.stem: A population has 8 existing leprosy cases among 100,000 people. The source marks the leprosy elimination level as <1 per 10,000 population. Using the source prevalence logic and that elimination threshold, which interpretation is correct?
options: The elimination level is not met
The prevalence cannot be interpreted from these data
questions.explanation: Eight existing cases in 100,000 people correspond to 0.8 per 10,000, which is below the source's leprosy elimination level of <1 per 10,000 population.

questions.stem: Routine clinical reporting captures mainly the visible tip of a disease iceberg. A programme wants both a surveillance approach aimed at hidden/missing cases and a method for detecting subclinical individuals. Which pairing matches the two source diagrams?
questions.explanation: The surveillance page labels sentinel surveillance as a way to identify hidden/missing cases, while the iceberg page labels screening as the method used to detect the hidden/submerged subclinical pool. They are two different tools, not synonyms.

questions.stem: Following an accident, a patient has permanent impairment, cannot perform routine activities, and has difficulty fulfilling his previous social role. Which intervention belongs to the prevention level directed at these established consequences?
questions.explanation: The patient has progressed from impairment to disability and difficulty fulfilling a social role. Tertiary prevention contains disability limitation and rehabilitation.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman requests Qdenga vaccination. The source identifies Qdenga as a live attenuated vaccine, while pregnancy is listed under live-vaccine contraindications. What follows from the source?
options: Qdenga should not be administered during pregnancy
Give Qdenga because it is tetravalent
questions.explanation: Qdenga is labelled live attenuated, while pregnancy is listed among contraindications to live vaccination.
questions.answer_label: Do not administer Qdenga during pregnancy
questions.answer: Qdenga should not be administered during pregnancy

questions.stem: An 18-month-old child is due for a 2 lakh IU vitamin A dose. The solution supplied contains 1 lakh IU/mL. How much solution is required?
questions.explanation: At this age the source shows a 2 lakh IU dose. The solution contains 1 lakh IU/mL. Formula: 2 lakh IU ÷ 1 lakh IU/mL = 2 mL.

questions.stem: A newborn is due for both BCG and hepatitis B vaccine. Which administration plan matches the birth schedule and the route/site table in the source?
options: BCG 0.5 mL IM in right arm + Hep B 0.05 mL intradermal in thigh
BCG 0.05 mL subcutaneous in right arm + Hep B 0.5 mL intradermal in left deltoid
BCG 0.05 mL intradermal over left deltoid + Hep B 0.5 mL IM in anterolateral thigh
BCG 0.5 mL intradermal in thigh + Hep B 0.05 mL subcutaneous in right arm
questions.explanation: Both vaccines are due at birth. The route/site table gives newborn BCG 0.05 mL intradermal over the left deltoid and hepatitis B 0.5 mL IM in the anterolateral thigh.
questions.answer_label: BCG 0.05 mL ID left deltoid + Hep B 0.5 mL IM anterolateral thigh
questions.answer: BCG 0.05 mL intradermal over left deltoid + Hep B 0.5 mL IM in anterolateral thigh
